title: A lookup (a join): each record reads the row of a second file that has its key
proves: <variable source="*.ent.csv" storage="data"> holds every row of a second file, and a script selects the row with the key of the current record
a key with no row in the second file gives None, and the script writes a default (UNKNOWN)
several records read the same row, and the first and the last row of the second file are found
an empty column of the found row stays empty text, and the script can replace it
the lookup variables and an unlisted source column are not output fields
a list comprehension spells the same lookup, and the order of the second file does not change the result
the lookup table in a <nestedKey> is an output field, a key of another type finds no row, a missing default fails the run, and <variable> has no where=

patch.old: script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}.get(branch_id)"
patch.new: script="([b for b in branches if b.branch_id == branch_id] or [None])[0]"

patch.old:
<variable name="branches" source="data/entity/branches.ent.csv" storage="data" distribution="ordered"/>
        <variable name="branch" script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}
patch.new:
<nestedKey name="branches" type="list" source="data/entity/branches.ent.csv" distribution="ordered"/>
        <variable name="branch" script="{b.branch_id: b for b in this.branches}

patch.old: <variable name="branch" script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}.get(branch_id)"/>
